title: From Farmland to Token
subtitle: How a regulated real-world asset becomes a compliant token on Redbelly Network, through Tokeniser

asset.name: An Australian farmland fund
asset.type: Registered fund (unit trust). Investors hold units in the fund.
asset.why: Tokeniser is built for Australian funds and companies. A farmland fund is a real, regulated structure that anyone can picture: land you can see, owned through units that investors hold. It lets the video show the difference between the asset (the farmland, which does not change) and the record of who owns it (which becomes a token).
asset.note: Illustrative example. Not a real fund. No prices, returns or performance are shown or implied.

audience: Someone with no crypto or finance background.

voice.dataset: Alba speech corpus, University of Edinburgh DataShare, CC BY 4.0

style_rules: Plain English, one idea per sentence.
No em dashes or en dashes, no emoji, no exclamation marks.
No price talk, returns, performance or investment advice.
No hype words such as elevate, seamless, unleash or revolutionize.
Every claim about Redbelly or Tokeniser is backed by a quote from the supplied resources.

scenes.title: The question

lines.vo: How does a real-world asset become a token? Let's follow one asset, step by step.

onscreen: From real-world asset to compliant token
scenes.visual: Dark slate opening. A token draws itself and fills with Tokeniser mint, the title appears, then a four stop journey rail (Set up, Investors, Issue, Transfer) draws in. The dark layer lifts away and the rail settles at the top right, where it tracks progress for the rest of the video.

scenes.title: The asset

lines.vo: Meet an Australian farmland fund. Investors hold its units, and the register sits across separate systems, updated after the fact.

scenes.visual: Isometric farmland builds up parcel by parcel inside a dashed frame that marks the fund. A row of unit tiles appears below it, linked to three investors. On the right, the register today appears as three separate documents (spreadsheet, email, admin system) with broken links between them and a clock.

claims.claim: Fund registers today are commonly kept across separate systems and updated after the fact.
claims.quote: Most fund registers are updated after the fact, across several systems that require manual reconciliation.

claims.claim: Tokeniser is built for Australian funds.
claims.quote: Give your Australian fund a global edge

scenes.title: What tokenisation means

lines.vo: Tokenisation records that ownership as digital tokens, with the fund's rules programmed in.

scenes.visual: The farmland stays where it is and the old register fades. The unit tiles lift and turn into tokens. A small rules badge settles onto each token.

claims.claim: Tokenisation records ownership as digital tokens and lets the issuer program the rules of the asset.
claims.quote: Tokenisation records ownership of financial products and services as digital tokens, and lets you program the rules of the asset.

scenes.title: Two layers

lines.vo: The manager uses Tokeniser, a familiar platform. Underneath runs Redbelly Network, Australia's public digital token infrastructure.

scenes.visual: A Tokeniser platform window slides in and the tokens settle into it. Then the dark Redbelly Network layer rises in underneath the window, with the Redbelly logo and a chain of blocks. These two layers stay on screen as the stage for the four steps.

claims.claim: Tokeniser is a familiar platform with Redbelly Network running underneath it, described as Australia's public digital token infrastructure.
claims.quote: Tokeniser gives you a familiar platform. Underneath it runs Redbelly Network, Australia's public digital token infrastructure

claims.claim: Tokeniser operates on Redbelly Network.
claims.quote: Tokeniser operates on Redbelly Network, Australia's public digital token infrastructure, with identity and eligibility built into the protocol.

scenes.title: Step 1. Set up

lines.vo: Step one: set up. The fund is verified, and its rules, like wholesale investors only, are encoded into the token.

scenes.visual: In the platform window, the fund setup card changes from Pending to Fund verified. Two rule chips, Wholesale investors only and Transfer restrictions, appear and fly to the token, which gains a rules badge and a lock.

claims.claim: Setup includes entity verification and defining compliance rules.
claims.quote: Complete entity verification, fund or company details, and administrator accounts.

claims.claim: Compliance rules are encoded into the token.
claims.quote: Compliance parameters are encoded into the token smart contract and can be updated on-chain.

claims.claim: Wholesale investor thresholds and transfer restrictions are configurable rules.
claims.quote: Foreign ownership limits, lock-up periods, and wholesale investor thresholds are all configurable compliance parameters.

scenes.title: Step 2. Investors

lines.vo: Step two: investors. Each is verified through Averer, then gets a wallet on Redbelly Network to hold tokens.

scenes.visual: A verification scan labelled Averer passes over three investor cards. Two investors are verified and their wallets drop onto the Redbelly Network layer. The third is not verified and gets no wallet and no tokens.

claims.claim: Investors are verified through Averer before they can transact.
claims.quote: Investors are verified by Averer before they can transact, with eligibility checks built into the protocol itself.

claims.claim: Onboarding covers identity verification, investor classification and a wallet.
claims.quote: Investors onboard to Tokeniser through a digital process: identity verification, investor classification under the Corporations Act, and wallet creation.

claims.claim: The wallet is on Redbelly Network and holds the investor's tokens.
claims.quote: The investor's wallet is a digital wallet on Redbelly Network. It holds the tokens representing their ownership interest.

claims.claim: Investors who are not verified cannot receive tokens.
claims.quote: Until onboarding is complete and the wallet is verified, tokens cannot be issued or transferred to that investor.

scenes.title: Step 3. Issue

lines.vo: Step three: issue. Tokens are minted on Redbelly Network into verified wallets, and the register updates immediately.

scenes.visual: A block on the Redbelly Network layer lights up and tokens are minted from it into the two verified wallets. At the same moment the register in the platform window fills in and marks each row Updated.

claims.claim: Tokens are minted on Redbelly Network and transferred to verified investor wallets.
claims.quote: Tokens are minted on Redbelly Network and transferred to the verified investor wallets.

claims.claim: The register updates immediately on issuance.
claims.quote: The on-chain register updates immediately to reflect each issuance.

scenes.title: Step 4. Transfer

lines.vo: Step four: transfer. Every transfer is checked against the rules first. A transfer to an ineligible investor is rejected.

scenes.visual: A token leaves the first wallet for the rules check in the platform window, addressed to an ineligible investor. The Wholesale investors only rule fails, the transfer is stamped Rejected and the token returns to its wallet. Nothing reaches the network.

claims.claim: Every transfer is checked against the rules before it is processed.
claims.quote: Every transfer is checked against configured compliance parameters before submission.

claims.claim: Transfers to ineligible investors are rejected.
claims.quote: Transfers to unverified wallets, ineligible investors, or in breach of restrictions are rejected.

scenes.title: Settlement

lines.vo: A compliant one settles on Redbelly in seconds. When investors hold their own wallets, transfer and payment complete together. Once confirmed, it is final.

scenes.visual: The same token is sent to an eligible investor. Both rules pass. On the Redbelly Network layer the token and the payment cross between the two wallets at the same block, which then locks and is marked Final.

claims.claim: Compliant transfers settle on Redbelly Network in seconds.
claims.quote: Compliant transfers settle atomically on Redbelly Network in seconds.

claims.claim: With wallets the investors hold themselves (non-custodial), transfer and payment complete together.
claims.quote: For non-custodial wallets, atomic settlements, transfer and payment complete simultaneously in seconds.

claims.claim: Once confirmed, a transaction on Redbelly is final and cannot be reversed.
claims.quote: Deterministic finality ensures transactions are confirmed once and cannot be reversed, providing certainty for financial markets

scenes.title: The record

lines.vo: Every check, transfer and rejection is recorded, ready for auditors and regulators.

scenes.visual: The platform window shows an audit log: a check, a transfer and a rejection, each marked Recorded, while matching blocks lock on the network layer. Two readers, Auditors and Regulators, connect to the log.

claims.claim: Every check, transfer and rejection is recorded and available to administrators, auditors and regulators.
claims.quote: Every compliance check, every transfer, and every rejection is recorded on-chain and in the platform's compliance log. This creates an immutable audit trail that is available to fund administrators, auditors, and regulators at any time.

scenes.title: Same asset, new record

lines.vo: Same farmland, same fund. Its units are now compliant tokens on Redbelly Network, issued through Tokeniser.

onscreen: Now compliant tokens on Redbelly Network
scenes.visual: The farmland returns at the top, unchanged, linked by dashed lines to the tokens held in the wallets on the Redbelly Network layer. All four steps on the rail are complete.

claims.claim: Tokeniser issues compliant tokens representing ownership interests on Redbelly Network.
claims.quote: Tokeniser issues digital tokens representing ownership interests on Redbelly Network blockchain.

claims.claim: Tokeniser provides compliant asset tokenisation.
claims.quote: Tokeniser Pty. Ltd. is an Australian company providing compliant asset tokenisation and management solutions.

onscreen: Illustrative example. General information only, not financial advice.

claims.claim: Tokeniser is built on Redbelly Network.
claims.quote: Built on Redbelly, Australia's public digital token infrastructure and the network chosen by Australia's central bank for its digital currency project.
